Samira V.: Hey team — quick question. My brother turned 27 this month and is on the plan as a dependent. He has a long-term disability and was receiving SSDI before he turned 26. Can I keep him on my medical and vision after he aged out?
Lina (People Ops): Hi Samira, thanks for asking — yes, dependents with qualifying disabilities can remain covered past the plan's age limit, but carriers need documentation.
Samira V.: What docs do they need? I have an SSA disability award letter and a recent physician letter. Is that enough?
Amrita K.: Usually carriers want two things: 1) proof of disability (SSA award letter or SSA determination) showing disability onset before the dependent reached the plan age limit; and 2) proof of continued dependency (proof of primary residence with you or evidence of financial support). A physician statement that confirms the condition and ongoing care is strongly recommended.
Samira V.: The SSA award letter shows onset date in 2023 (before they turned 26) and the physician letter is signed this month. For residency I can provide a recent joint lease with my brother's name and a utility bill.
Benefits Admin: That should be fine. When you submit, include: SSA award letter, current physician statement (on letterhead with diagnosis and statement of need), proof of residence (lease + utility) and a short attestation from you about financial support.
Samira V.: Is there a deadline to submit these? His birthday already passed but I reported within the 31-day grace window after they aged out.
Lina (People Ops): Because you reported promptly (within our internal 31-day window) we'll request the carrier to continue coverage pending verification. Upload the docs within 60 days so carriers can finalize. If carriers need more info they'll ask; we can escalate.
Ken L.: Payroll note: If coverage stays active retro to the day after the dependent would have aged out, payroll will continue deductions. If carrier denies the extension retro, payroll will adjust and may issue a refund for premiums taken after the denial. We'll coordinate once Benefits confirms carrier decision.
Samira V.: Secure upload link? I don't want to email SSA docs.
people-ops-bot: Secure upload link generated: https://benefits.redwood.com/secure-upload/SV-1925000000 (expires in 14 days).
Amrita K.: In the upload form choose "Dependent - disabled over 26" and include the dependent's DOB, the date they turned 26, and a short note about onset date shown on SSA doc.
Samira V.: If SSA award letter is a PDF with most info redacted, is that a problem?
Benefits Admin: Carriers sometimes need the SSA award letter unredacted for dates and SSA claim numbers. If sensitive info needs to be redactd, include a cover note explaining why and provide the claim number separately if available. We can request carrier flexibility but unredacted docs speed verification.
Samira V.: Got it. If carrier requests additional info, how long does that take?
Lina (People Ops): It varies by carrier; usually 5-20 business days after submission. We'll DM you and also update case notes in the upload portal.
Samira V.: Will this qualify as a QLE allowing plan changes?
Amrita K.: No, this is a dependent status verification. It doesn't trigger an open enrollment-style QLE to change plans. You can still make plan changes only during open enrollment or if you have a separate QLE.
Samira V.: Uploaded SSA letter, physician statement, lease, and utility bill.
people-ops-bot: Case created: PO-8344 - Adult dependent disability continuation. Benefits admin notified.
Benefits Admin: Received. We'll submit to carrier today and loop back when carrier confirms. Please keep an eye on your email; carriers sometimes send direct requests.
Samira V.: Thank you — really appreciate the fast help.
